review.summary: The paper proposes a difficulty-aware sampler that only requests teacher labels for examples whose student-side predictive entropy exceeds a threshold. It claims to match dense distillation accuracy within 0.4 points while reducing teacher compute by 51% on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, and a 3M-example text classification benchmark.

strengths.comment: The difficulty-aware sampler is an intuitive, low-cost addition to standard distillation pipelines.

weaknesses.comment: The entropy threshold is reported as a single value; there is no ablation across {0.1, 0.5, 0.9} so robustness to the threshold cannot be judged.

questions.question: How is teacher compute measured: wall-clock or FLOPs?

suggestions.suggestion: Add a random-subset distillation baseline to isolate the contribution of the difficulty-aware criterion.
